title: Data Steward role and scope

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Option 1 - Business Data Steward: adopt this DMBOK2 steward type as the label for the target role (business professionals, most often subject matter experts, accountable for a subset of data and working with stakeholders to define and control it) [DMBOK2-C03-23, DMBOK2-C03-24]. Fits a steward who works with SMEs and Data Owners on Investment Operations definitions and quality; implies business-side accountability for a data subset.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Option 2 - Enterprise Data Steward: adopt this type instead, because it describes oversight of a data domain across business functions [DMBOK2-C03-22]. Fits a steward who spans definitions, mappings, lineage and quality across the whole Investment Operations data domain; implies a wider remit than a single subset.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Option 3 - keep the neutral title 'Data Steward' and add only a one-line note that the DMBOK2 stewardship definition and focus areas are general industry context [DMBOK2-C03-14]; the DMBOK2 says stewards may be differentiated by place or focus and that terms such as custodian or trustee are used for steward-like functions, so no single label is required [DMBOK2-C03-20, DMBOK2-C03-15].

recommendation: Option 3 - least change; the DMBOK2 allows steward-like titles, so keep 'Data Steward' with a one-line note and adopt a steward type later if the organisation does.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 3 - least change; the DMBOK2 allows steward-like titles, so keep 'Data Steward' with a one-line note and adopt a steward type later if the organisation does. Applied in README.md note and docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 1 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Governance bodies, escalation path and the named human governance owner

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Option 1 - single accountable owner (virtual model): name one human governance owner and a deputy as the escalation and approval endpoint, optionally titled Chief Data Steward since the DMBOK2 lets such a steward chair governance bodies in lieu of a CDO [DMBOK2-C03-21], within a governance team that may be virtual with specific accountabilities [DMBOK2-C03-04]; record the role in a short operating framework and accountabilities statement [DMBOK2-C03-32] and identify the executive sponsor the DMBOK2 expects [DMBOK2-C03-02]. Lowest overhead; no layered escalation.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Option 2 - council-based escalation ladder: adopt the DMBOK2 pattern in which stewardship teams settle what they can, escalations are logged, and unresolved issues go up to a Data Governance Council and then to corporate governance or management [DMBOK2-C03-44, DMBOK2-C03-46], with the escalation procedure published [DMBOK2-C03-61]. Needs a council to exist; level names and members are shown in Table 4 and Figure 20, which are unverifiable from text.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Option 3 - council with delegated steering committee: as Option 2, but the council delegates enforcement of policies to a Data Stewardship Steering Committee [DMBOK2-C03-40], reflecting the DMBOK2 view that governance work is often divided among several committees with different purposes and levels of oversight [DMBOK2-C03-12]. Suits a larger programme than the project currently describes.

options.label: Option 4
options.description: Option A - single accountable executive: name one senior executive as governance owner and escalation point, acting as sponsor for the capability. The DMBOK2 describes a single top accountable leader as making decisions easier and accountability clear, and names an executive sponsor (ideally the CDO) for oversight. Backed by DMBOK2-C16-10 and DMBOK2-C15-20.

options.label: Option 5
options.description: Option B - decision-making governance forum: route escalations to a Data Governance Steering Committee with working groups, either newly created or an existing committee used cautiously, and require that it is a decision-making body. Backed by DMBOK2-C16-22, DMBOK2-C16-13 and DMBOK2-C16-23.

options.label: Option 6
options.description: Option C - documented accountability map: keep the current structure and record Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed roles for Factory sign-off, operational sign-off and override authority in a RACI matrix, which the DMBOK2 presents as adding accountability without changing organisation charts. Backed by DMBOK2-C16-08 and DMBOK2-C16-09.

recommendation: Option 1 - matches governance decision GD-01 (one accountable Project Owner, Data Steward as reviewer) and adds a deputy for escalation.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - matches governance decision GD-01 (one accountable Project Owner, Data Steward as reviewer) and adds a deputy for escalation. Applied in docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 2 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Governance reporting and metrics

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Option 1 - adopt the DMBOK2 metric groups: structure governance reporting under value, effectiveness and sustainability headings, map the HANDOFF.md success criteria into effectiveness and sustainability, and add value measures (business objectives, risk reduction, operational efficiency) [DMBOK2-C03-65, DMBOK2-C03-66, DMBOK2-C03-67, DMBOK2-C03-68].

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Option 2 - governance scorecard: define a periodic scorecard of governance activity and policy compliance, with issue trends by location and root cause, reported to the accountable governance body, and include data quality measurement reports [DMBOK2-C03-63, DMBOK2-C03-45, DMBOK2-C03-60].

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Option 3 - defer and record: keep the HANDOFF.md success criteria as system-level criteria only, record that programme-level stewardship metrics are deferred to the organisation's own governance metrics, and revisit as the programme matures, since the DMBOK2 expects metrics to change with maturity [DMBOK2-C03-64].

recommendation: Option 3 - defer programme-level metrics until operational agents exist; keep HANDOFF.md success criteria as system-level criteria and record the deferral.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 3 - defer programme-level metrics until operational agents exist; keep HANDOFF.md success criteria as system-level criteria and record the deferral. Applied in docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 3 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Business definitions and their approval lifecycle

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Adopt the DMBOK2 example status path (candidate, approved, published, replaced or retired) as the definition-status vocabulary in the Definition & CDE contract and any future definitions/ records, with a human approval gate on each change; costs a schema, contract and test update and a decision on who approves each transition (DMBOK2-C12-63, DMBOK2-C12-61).

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Keep the single DRAFT-NOT-APPROVED gate in this repository and leave published and replaced or retired states to the status model of the glossary system once it is chosen, treating the DMBOK2 path as an example of more mature governance; costs nothing now but leaves later lifecycle stages undefined here (DMBOK2-C12-62, DMBOK2-C12-22).

recommendation: Option 2 - keep the single DRAFT-NOT-APPROVED gate until a glossary system is chosen (backlog P4-04), then adopt its status model.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 2 - keep the single DRAFT-NOT-APPROVED gate until a glossary system is chosen (backlog P4-04), then adopt its status model. Applied in docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 4 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Critical data elements: criteria, designation and evidence

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Criticality drivers as the starting checklist: draft the CDE-criteria policy around the DMBOK2 common drivers (data required for regulatory reporting, financial reporting, business policy, ongoing operations or business strategy; Master Data critical by definition), assessed through consuming processes, the reports the data appears in, and financial, regulatory or reputational risk. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-05, DMBOK2-C13-06 and DMBOK2-C13-07; DMBOK2-C13-04 notes the drivers vary by industry, so the organisation would tailor the list.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Leaner prioritisation factors: start with the three factors DMBOK2 uses for ranking (regulatory requirements, financial value, direct impact on customers) and make a ranked list of data the policy's output. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-23 and DMBOK2-C13-24. Simpler to approve first time, but it omits the business-policy, ongoing-operations and strategy drivers in the first option.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Policy form: whichever criteria set is chosen, record it in a governed Data Quality policy using the DMBOK2 policy outline (purpose, scope and applicability; definitions; responsibilities; reporting; implementation) rather than leaving the criteria inside the agent contract. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-60, with DMBOK2-C13-59 for who identifies critical data.

recommendation: Option 1 - use the DMBOK2 criticality drivers as the starting CDE checklist, and record the result in a governed policy as in Option 3.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - use the DMBOK2 criticality drivers as the starting CDE checklist, and record the result in a governed policy as in Option 3. Applied in docs/CDE-CRITERIA-POLICY.md (draft, pending owner review).

title: Metadata management: repository, ownership and Stewardship as Code

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Hybrid: keep the version-controlled repository for steward-added governance metadata only (candidate and approved definitions, CDE evidence, decisions, links) and point to the glossary, catalog and source systems for everything else; costs a link convention and the effort of joining repository entries with source results at query time (DMBOK2-C12-41, DMBOK2-C12-42).

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Centralized: treat the repository as the single store holding copies of governance metadata taken from the source systems, giving one searchable store; costs the replication processes needed to keep copies current, and the DMBOK2 notes that teams with limited IT resources or seeking maximum automation may avoid it (DMBOK2-C12-36, DMBOK2-C12-37, DMBOK2-C12-38).

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Distributed: hold no copies in the repository and have agents read the authoritative systems on demand, recording only references; metadata is retrieved from its source at the time of use, but there is no place for steward-added or manual entries (DMBOK2-C12-39, DMBOK2-C12-40).

recommendation: Option 1 - hybrid: keep the repository for steward-added governance metadata only and link to source systems for the rest.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - hybrid: keep the repository for steward-added governance metadata only and link to source systems for the rest. Applied in docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 5 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Data quality dimensions (the taxonomy)

options.label: Option 1
options.description: DAMA UK core six: use completeness, uniqueness, timeliness, validity, accuracy and consistency as the starting set for the organisation's own versioned taxonomy; these are the examples docs/IMPLEMENTATION-SEQUENCE.md Phase 0b item 2 already names. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-12; DMBOK2-C13-13 shows DAMA UK keeps other quality characteristics outside the six, so the taxonomy would need to say where those sit.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: English inherent/pragmatic split: organise the taxonomy in two tiers, inherent characteristics versus pragmatic ones, so dimensions that do not depend on data use are kept apart from those that do, which fits the project's fitness-for-purpose principle. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-11.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Strong-Wang consumer-perception set: adopt the 15 dimensions in four categories if the organisation wants dimensions framed around how data consumers perceive quality; it is a larger set, and DMBOK2-C13-15 warns that some dimensions rest on context or subjective interpretation. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-09.

options.label: Option 4
options.description: Redman data-structure set: adopt Redman's grouping (data model, data values, representation) only if the taxonomy must also cover the quality of the model and of how data is recorded, not just stored values. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-10.

options.label: Option 5
options.description: Own set with mapping: define an organisation-specific set and record a mapping to the published sets, relying on DMBOK2's statement that no single set is agreed and applying the chosen dimensions consistently in rules. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-14 and DMBOK2-C13-30.

recommendation: Option 1 - DAMA UK core six, as already accepted in governance decision GD-04 (a proposal until the organisation confirms or replaces it).
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - DAMA UK core six, as already accepted in governance decision GD-04 (a proposal until the organisation confirms or replaces it). Applied in docs/DATA-QUALITY-FRAMEWORK.md section 1 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Quality rules, expectations and candidate controls and tests

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Rule-type field: add a rule_type vocabulary taken from DMBOK2's simple business rule types (definitional conformance, value presence and record completeness, format compliance, value domain membership, range conformance, mapping conformance, consistency, accuracy verification, uniqueness verification, timeliness validation) so every candidate rule is classified, with definitional conformance tying a test back to the business definition. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-18 and DMBOK2-C13-19.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Pre-approval checklist: have each candidate rule carry the DMBOK2 rule-management attributes the project does not yet require (consistent documentation from a template, expressed through an approved dimension, tested against actual data, confirmed by subject-matter experts) before it reaches the Data Steward. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-30, DMBOK2-C13-31, DMBOK2-C13-32 and DMBOK2-C13-49.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Rule-discovery intake (optional): add a separately labelled path for rules inferred from processes or data rather than taken from an approved expectation, always tagged as agent inference needing SME confirmation, instead of leaving undocumented rules unaddressed. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-25 and DMBOK2-C13-32.

recommendation: Option 2 - a pre-approval checklist on each candidate rule is the smallest change that raises rule quality before it reaches the Data Steward.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 2 - a pre-approval checklist on each candidate rule is the smallest change that raises rule quality before it reaches the Data Steward. Applied in docs/DATA-QUALITY-FRAMEWORK.md section 2 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Quality measurement, monitoring and control coverage

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Coverage matrix from the SLA scoping list: define coverage as, for each critical data element, which dimensions have an approved rule and threshold in which systems of the data value chain, mirroring the DMBOK2 SLA list of covered elements and per-element, per-dimension, per-system expectations. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-46 and DMBOK2-C13-33.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Risk-led coverage: prioritise gaps where relationships have failed before and where similar functions exist, following DMBOK2's guidance on where to place measurements. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-34 and DMBOK2-C13-33.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Measurement-level attribute: record for each control whether it measures at data element, record or data-set level, so coverage reports can show gaps by measurement level. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-36 (the technique table behind this, Table 31, is not in the text).

recommendation: Option 1 - coverage matrix of critical data element by dimension by system gives a testable definition of coverage.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - coverage matrix of critical data element by dimension by system gives a testable definition of coverage. Applied in docs/DATA-QUALITY-FRAMEWORK.md section 3 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Quality issue and exception management

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Minimum issue record: give the packet routed to a human the fields DMBOK2 lists for tracked issues (issue description, root causes, remediation options, decision), with the decision owner being a business data owner. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-41 and DMBOK2-C13-40.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Standard vocabulary and clustering keys: adopt a controlled issue classification (related to docs/ARCHITECTURE-RISKS.md Open Question 6 on exception structure) and use DMBOK2's issue metrics as clustering and reporting keys: dimension, business function, status, priority and severity, time to resolve. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-42, DMBOK2-C13-43 and DMBOK2-C13-61.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Escalation rule: define routing urgency by the impact, duration and urgency of an issue rather than by agent judgement. Backed by DMBOK2-C13-44.

recommendation: Option 1 - a minimum issue record (description, root causes, remediation options, decision) is the smallest useful change.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - a minimum issue record (description, root causes, remediation options, decision) is the smallest useful change. Applied in docs/DATA-QUALITY-FRAMEWORK.md section 4 and schemas/quality-issue.schema.json (draft, pending owner review).

title: Reference and master data stewardship

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Name reference data and master data as explicit content areas of the Investment Operations Context Agent, with no new agent or artefact type, in line with the DMBOK2 view that architecture typically starts with master data areas [DMBOK2-C04-17] and that integration is critical to reference and master data management [DMBOK2-C08-02]; this is the cheapest change but gives stewards context about the data, not stewardship of it.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Add a reference-and-master-data register as a Stewardship-as-Code artefact that names each data hub and the match, merge, survivorship and trust rules governing it, using the DMBOK2 hub and master data rule vocabulary [DMBOK2-C08-08] [DMBOK2-C08-20]; this brings the data itself under steward review and human approval but needs an owner and upkeep that the project has not assigned.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Reference Data first: add a small versioned register of the Reference Data sets that matter to Investment Operations, recording for each the steward name, originating organisation, update frequency and schedule, and the processes that use it, starting with the most important sets and leaving the owner to choose whether the steward maintains values directly or facilitates others (backed by DMBOK2-C10-34, DMBOK2-C10-30, DMBOK2-C10-32 and DMBOK2-C10-33); this is a governance document rather than a new agent, and its cost is a human-maintained register.

options.label: Option 4
options.description: One Master Data domain first: choose a single Investment Operations master data domain, begin with a handful of attributes, and define who reviews match-and-merge exceptions as a steward task before any tooling is considered (backed by DMBOK2-C10-21 and DMBOK2-C10-29); the cost is a deeper stewardship commitment for one domain, with matching, merging and the choice of system of record staying with the Data Steward and the appropriate human owner.

options.label: Option 5
options.description: Context-agent scope only: name reference data and master data as content areas of the Investment Operations Context Agent in ARCHITECTURE.md, keep the INTERNAL DOCUMENTED POSITION and GENERAL INDUSTRY CONTEXT distinction, and define the project's use of 'reconciliation' so it is not confused with consolidating source records (backed by DMBOK2-C10-08, DMBOK2-C10-01 and DMBOK2-C10-22); this is the cheapest change but defines no stewardship duties, register or coverage check, so the gap stays partly open.

recommendation: Option 1 - name reference and master data as content areas of the Investment Operations Context Agent with no new agent or artefact type.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - name reference and master data as content areas of the Investment Operations Context Agent with no new agent or artefact type. Applied in ARCHITECTURE.md content areas and docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 6 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Data classification, confidentiality and permitted use, including AI processing

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Adopt a confidentiality scale only, taking two or more of the DMBOK2 example levels (DMBOK2-C07-06) as a provisional label, to be replaced by the organisation's own scheme once found (DMBOK2-C07-09), that agents may propose and the Data Steward assigns (DMBOK2-C07-10) and records as metadata (DMBOK2-C07-16); the cost is one optional field named differently from the capability 'classification' already used in schemas/agent-contract.schema.json, plus labelling rules, with schema, contract and test changes made together.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Adopt the DMBOK2 risk classification of critical, high and moderate risk data (DMBOK2-C07-03) as the label instead of confidentiality levels; the cost is the same single field plus class definitions the organisation would have to write for its own Investment Operations content.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Adopt two separate labels, a confidentiality level plus regulatory categories (DMBOK2-C07-05 and DMBOK2-C07-06), because DMBOK2 treats confidentiality and regulation as distinct drivers of restriction; the cost is two fields and a category list that must be written and kept current.

recommendation: Option 1 - a provisional confidentiality scale that agents may propose and the Data Steward assigns, replaced by the organisation's scheme once found.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - a provisional confidentiality scale that agents may propose and the Data Steward assigns, replaced by the organisation's scheme once found. Applied in docs/DATA-CLASSIFICATION.md and schemas/evidence.schema.json (draft, pending owner review).

title: Stewardship operating model and organisation structure

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Option A - decentralized, functional-level steward (the current de facto position): record that the Investment Operations Data Steward works at functional level in a decentralized model and name the forum used for collaboration; the DMBOK2 notes most organisations start here but that data ownership is harder to define. Backed by DMBOK2-C16-12, DMBOK2-C16-33 and DMBOK2-C16-07.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Option B - network model: keep the single steward and add a RACI matrix linking the steward, Data Owners, SMEs, operations teams and the governance owner, which the DMBOK2 says adds accountability without changing organisation charts. Backed by DMBOK2-C16-08 and DMBOK2-C16-09.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Option C - hybrid model: pair the business-unit steward with a central Center of Excellence and an executive steering committee, as in the DMBOK2 hybrid pattern. Backed by DMBOK2-C16-11.

recommendation: Option 1 - record the current decentralized, functional-level steward position and name the collaboration forum; revisit if the programme grows.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 1 - record the current decentralized, functional-level steward position and name the collaboration forum; revisit if the programme grows. Applied in docs/STEWARDSHIP-FRAMEWORK.md section 7 (draft, pending owner review).

title: Capability measurement and success criteria

options.label: Option 1
options.description: Option A - scoped assessment with a published framework: choose a published data management maturity framework (the DMBOK2 names CMMI-DMM, the financial-services DCAM and others), evaluate several before choosing, and limit the first assessment to Investment Operations data stewardship; the DMBOK2 cautions that a baseline understanding and some organisational maturity are needed first. Backed by DMBOK2-C15-07, DMBOK2-C15-08, DMBOK2-C15-09, DMBOK2-C15-01, DMBOK2-C15-12 and DMBOK2-C15-02.

options.label: Option 2
options.description: Option B - DMBOK2-based checklist self-assessment: use the DMBOK2 knowledge areas, activities and deliverables as a fast checklist, with criteria grouped by activity, tools, standards, and people and resources and scored against generic maturity levels, keeping the model intact when tailoring. Backed by DMBOK2-C15-17, DMBOK2-C15-18, DMBOK2-C15-05, DMBOK2-C15-06, DMBOK2-C15-04 and DMBOK2-C15-11.

options.label: Option 3
options.description: Option C - turn the Success criteria into ongoing measures: keep them as the target state and rate each one against a stated baseline on a published review schedule, without adopting a formal maturity scale. Backed by DMBOK2-C15-14, DMBOK2-C15-23 and DMBOK2-C15-16.

recommendation: Option 3 - turn the HANDOFF.md success criteria into ongoing measures against a stated baseline, without adopting a formal maturity scale yet.
decision: Accepted 2026-10-27 by the project owner as recommended: Option 3 - turn the HANDOFF.md success criteria into ongoing measures against a stated baseline, without adopting a formal maturity scale yet. Applied in docs/SUCCESS-MEASURES.md (draft, pending owner review).
